2_Introduction: The devices exhibited an increased PCE from 24.7998% to 24.7998%, with a VOC of 1.1627 V, FF of 81.189%, and JSC of 26.272 mA/cm². Starting with a Cs0.05MA0.08FA0.87PbI3.0 (1.65 mol/L) solution, the perovskite precursor was carefully crafted for optimal performance. The deposition process involved a two-step spin sequence (1000 rpm/5 s and 5500 rpm/30 s) to achieve a controlled film thickness. A total of 150 µL of CB was dripped onto the center of film at 15 s before the end of spin-coating. Subsequently, the samples were annealed at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The triple-cation Cs0.05MA0.08FA0.87PbI3 perovskite, with its optimized A-site composition, enhances phase stability and minimizes ion migration by tailoring the tolerance factor within the ideal range for structural integrity. The precursor concentration of 1.65 mol/L, coupled with a precisely timed two-step spin-coating sequence (1000 rpm for 5 s followed by 5500 rpm for 30 s), ensures controlled film thickness and uniform liquid film spreading, which are critical for homogeneous nucleation. The introduction of 150 µL of chlorobenzene antisolvent at 15 s before the end of the spin-coating stage rapidly triggers supersaturation, directing the crystallization pathway towards the formation of a dense, pinhole-free morphology with reduced defect density. Subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 15 minutes drives solvent evaporation, promotes grain growth, and passivates residual defects, thereby enhancing carrier lifetimes and reducing non-radiative recombination losses. This meticulous control over crystallization dynamics and film formation collectively underpins the high performance, yielding a champion device with a VOC of 1.1627 V, a JSC of 26.272 mA/cm², an FF of 81.189%, and a PCE of 24.7998%.
